name: Wolves in the Throne Room
label: Southern Lord
lede: Brothers Nathan and Aaron Weaver took black metal to an abandoned farm outside Olympia, played it by firelight, and kept saying no to the rock and roll machine.

eras.title: A cabin on Calliope Farm
eras.text: Nathan and Aaron Weaver play black metal in a falling-down cabin on an abandoned farm outside Olympia, Washington. Corpse paint, pseudonyms and Satanic imagery are out from the start.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wolves in the Throne Room · PopMatters
years.h: Two brothers hold a first practice in a falling-down cabin
years.p: [[Nathan Weaver|497bb953-3e90-423a-a60f-67b39cfc8cc8]] and [[Aaron Weaver|18cd9eb0-f3f9-4e81-95fa-003e0c089c96]] start Wolves in the Throne Room on Calliope Farm, an abandoned, overgrown property outside Olympia, Washington.
years.xp:
Aaron later described the band's aim as uncovering the spiritual and energetic reality of a place, which is why the Pacific Northwest landscape is the point rather than the backdrop.

They favored crust, doom and Norwegian and American black metal, and rejected corpse paint, pseudonyms and Satanic imagery from the start.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wolves in the Throne Room
years.h: A black CD-R wrapped in fur, with moss in the lyric sheet
years.p: The self-released 2004 demo goes out in that packaging.
years.xp: Guitarist [[Nick Paul|edb4fa5d-67b9-4672-94b4-9d5dbc0a38b0]], met through the local scene and a fan of Death, Bolt Thrower and Swans, played on it and left shortly after it was recorded.

years.h: Nick Paul is gone soon after the first demo
years.p: The guitarist, who had joined around 2003, leaves shortly after the band records its 2004 demo.

eras.title: Eleven hundred dollars and a pregnant guest
eras.text: Rick Dahlin joins, the band plays San Francisco to raise money, and a debut gets made for $1,100. Southern Lord notices.

years.h: Rick Dahlin brings the band to three
years.p: [[Rick Dahlin|92730c72-0b59-4721-a85f-a097c7214eef]] joins on guitar in early 2005, and the trio starts a second demo that includes two songs later heard on the debut album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wolves in the Throne Room · Wikipedia: Diadem of 12 Stars
years.h: Diadem of 12 Stars costs $1,100 to make
years.p: Tim Green records the debut at Louder Studios in San Francisco, and Vendlus Records releases it.
years.xp:
The band played San Francisco shows to raise the money and borrowed gear from the local band Ludicra. Jamie Myers of Hammers of Misfortune sang on it while nine months pregnant.

Pitchfork said the inclusion of folk and goth sets them apart from the pack.

years.h: Southern Lord hears Diadem and signs the band
years.p: Southern Lord signs Wolves in the Throne Room in late 2006 and reissues the debut on vinyl.
years.xp: The band re-issued Diadem of 12 Stars again in 2016 through its own label, Artemisia Records.

eras.title: Synths, tape and firelight
eras.text: Two albums in two years, analog synths, a producer who understands tape, and a live show lit by fire.

years.cap: Promo shoot from the Two Hunters era
years.src: Wikipedia: Two Hunters · Wikipedia: Wolves in the Throne Room
years.h: Randall Dunn brings analog synths to Two Hunters
years.p: First album with producer [[Randall Dunn|f2be6d74-fac1-4199-9ddc-f3f280630994]], built on a Korg Polysix and a Minimoog, and the first on Southern Lord.
years.xp:
Persian classical vocalist [[Jessika Kenney|d7e40021-e86e-4f64-85d5-6c36770fd2f3]] sings on "Cleansing" and "I Will Lay Down My Bones Among the Rocks and Roots." The vinyl carries a much longer "Cleansing" and the extra track "To Reveal."

Pitchfork gave it 7.9. Wikipedia says it put the band at the front of North American black metal.

years.h: Rick Dahlin leaves after two years
years.p: The guitarist's time in the band ends around 2007; Wikipedia dates it 2005 to 2007.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wolves in the Throne Room
years.h: Roadburn, by firelight
years.p: The band plays Roadburn in 2008 and again in 2009, and the festival later issues Live at Roadburn 2008.
years.xp: The band insists on firelit shows, outdoors or in, and bans flash photography. Guitarist and bassist [[Will Lindsay|e6f0e493-c32c-4f60-a204-33079b520b15]] joins for 2008 to 2009. They also play Hellfest, Graspop and Roskilde.

years.h: Will Lindsay becomes the third member
years.p: Lindsay joins on guitar and bass for the touring years around Black Cascade.

years.h: Black Cascade: recorded live-first, onto tape
years.p: Four tracks in about 50 minutes, with an opener named for Caspar David Friedrich's painting Wanderer above the Sea of Fog.
years.xp:
Aaron Weaver told The Obelisk that recording onto tape "makes things a lot more difficult," and that the record was live-first, unlike the studio-built Two Hunters. Randall Dunn produced again.

Reviews split: PopMatters gave it 8/10, Pitchfork 4.5.

years.big: "We'll do it on our own terms and we'll do it as long as it suits us"
years.h: Aaron Weaver on the rock and roll machine
years.p: In a 2009 interview with The Obelisk, Aaron Weaver says the band won't play along with the rock and roll machine.
years.xp:
He called touring "a big compromise" because he is "the most interested in focusing on our homestead."

The band toured the US and Europe with Sunn O))), Earth and Weedeater. Aaron also told The Obelisk that corporate festival sponsorship made him uneasy, naming Scion's marketing as the part he found most unnerving.

years.h: Malevolent Grain EP brings Jamie Myers back
years.p: The EP comes out on Southern Lord in 2009, with Myers back on vocals.

years.h: Will Lindsay leaves, and the brothers are two again
years.p: His time as third member ends in 2009.

eras.title: Two brothers and a fire
eras.text: Down to the Weavers, the band writes Celestial Lineage, and Godspeed You! Black Emperor pick them for All Tomorrow's Parties.

years.cap: Live at Tivoli Helling, Utrecht, May 2010
years.src: Wikipedia: Wolves in the Throne Room
years.h: Godspeed You! Black Emperor pick them for ATP
years.p: Godspeed curate the All Tomorrow's Parties festival in Minehead, England, and put Wolves in the Throne Room on the bill.

years.cap: The Weaver brothers, Celestial Lineage press photo, 2011
years.h: With no third guitarist, the brothers make Celestial Lineage
years.p: The first album written and recorded as a duo, again with Randall Dunn, with vocals from Jessika Kenney.
years.xp:
Recorded at Dunn's Aleph Studio. Kenney also sings choir parts, plays organ and wrote lyrics. NPR premiered "Woodland Cathedral" on August 9.

Brandon Stosuy of Pitchfork called it "American black metal's idiosyncratic defining record of 2011." Metacritic: 87 out of 100. AllMusic found it an "immersive, transcendental whole."

years.h: The Bell House, Brooklyn, on the eve of the album
years.p: A show at the Bell House on September 12, 2011 is later released as Live at the Bell House 9.12.11 (2015).

years.h: BBC Session 2011 Anno Domini goes out on Southern Lord
years.p: The live BBC session was recorded in 2011 and released in 2013.

eras.title: Artemisia Records and a studio in the woods
eras.text: The brothers start their own label, build a studio near Olympia, make a dark ambient record with no metal on it, then go back to black metal.

years.h: Celestite has no metal on it
years.p: A drone-based dark ambient companion to Celestial Lineage, with no vocals, on the band's own Artemisia Records.
years.xp: Randall Dunn recorded it at AVAST and Owl Lodge, with extra recording by Aaron Weaver at Owl Lodge. It uses synthesizers, guitars and a Serge modulator, plus French horns, trombones and flutes.

years.h: The debut comes back, remastered
years.p: Diadem of 12 Stars is remastered and reissued in June 2016, with a North American tour.

years.h: Thrice Woven lands three days early
years.p: Back to black metal on Artemisia, with Norse myth in it and a third guitarist, Kody Keyworth.
years.xp:
Aaron said the music was ready to flow out. They built a studio in the Olympia woods, called Owl Lodge, and started Artemisia so they would not have to travel to a city to record. Anna von Hausswolff and Steve Von Till guest.

Metacritic: 76 out of 100. Decibel named it "Best New Noise."

years.h: Kody Keyworth is invited to join mid-recording
years.p: Keyworth had toured with the band for six years. The brothers ask him to join officially partway through the Thrice Woven sessions.

years.cap: Live at With Full Force, Ferropolis, Germany, June 2018
years.h: Metal Hammer names them Best Underground Band
years.p: The Golden Gods award is handed out in London. The band then tours with Enslaved on the Decibel tour, and with Behemoth and At the Gates.

eras.title: Century Media, Relapse and Dimmu Borgir
eras.text: A bass player joins, two bigger labels follow, and a European tour opens with Dimmu Borgir. The farm stays.

years.h: Galen Baudhuin joins on bass
years.p: Bassist and vocalist [[Galen Baudhuin|f5edde0f-6623-4d29-a36e-f32cdc727542]] becomes a member and plays on Primordial Arcana.

years.h: Century Media signs them
years.p: Century Media Records signs the band, which has put out its own records on Artemisia since 2014.

years.h: They open for Dimmu Borgir and Amorphis across Europe
years.p: The European tour runs in January 2020.

yt: Live at Fire in the Mountains, 2022
years.h: Relapse puts out Primordial Arcana
years.p: The single "Mountain Magick" previews it on June 10.

years.cap: Live at Dark Troll Open Air, Bornstedt, Germany
years.h: Crypt of Ancestral Knowledge follows, as an EP
years.p: Relapse releases the EP on September 29, after the single "Twin Mouthed Spring" on August 16.
